actions.title: Read the learner-owned decision boundary
actions.instruction: Use the selected harness to establish the boundary before any drafting: the learner chooses and approves the ADR and decision-log boundary; the agent may analyze and draft but may not make that decision.
actions.rationale: The exercise records a real architectural choice without assigning decision authority to the agent.

variants.command: Read the P03 decision boundary. I choose and approve the ADR/log boundary; do not choose it for me.
Read the P03 decision boundary. I choose and approve the ADR/log boundary; do not choose it for me.
Read the P03 decision boundary. I choose and approve the ADR/log boundary; do not choose it for me.

actions.expected_result: The learner and agent share the boundary: analysis and drafting can be delegated, but the decision and approval remain learner-owned.
actions.recovery: If the agent selects an alternative or commits before learner approval, preserve the attempt and reset rather than treating that action as learner evidence.
actions.evidence: Check can inspect the resulting artifacts but cannot authenticate who chose or approved them.

actions.title: Keep prepared identity private
actions.instruction: Use the selected harness to keep identity within Academy's prepared boundary. Academy records the display-safe Git author name from %an; do not paste an email address or a rejected name into the ADR, log, or chat.
actions.rationale: The lesson needs attributable committed evidence without retaining unnecessary personal data.

variants.command: Keep the prepared author identity private. Do not request, display, or record an email address.
Keep the prepared author identity private. Do not request, display, or record an email address.
Keep the prepared author identity private. Do not request, display, or record an email address.

actions.expected_result: The ADR and log use only the prepared display-safe name, while no learner email is retained or rendered.
actions.recovery: If the prepared name is rejected, preserve the error and retry through Academy; never echo the rejected value as evidence.
actions.evidence: Check reads committed author metadata and artifact attribution, not a learner-supplied identity transcript.

actions.title: Prepare the numbered P03 attempt
actions.instruction: P03 is public, guided, and runnable in this preview. Run the installed Academy Prepare command outside the learner checkout; do not substitute source checkout behavior.
actions.rationale: Prepare establishes the verifier-owned attempt baseline and branch before the learner creates evidence.
actions.expected_result: Academy prints the prepared attempt branch and baseline without changing the decision artifacts yet.
actions.recovery: If P03 is not guided in the installed release or Prepare fails, preserve the message and do not invent an attempt number or branch.
actions.evidence: The prepared baseline lets Check compare the final committed ADR and append-only log state.

actions.title: Inspect the occupied decision context
actions.instruction: In a native terminal at the prepared clone root, inspect ADR-0003 and the current decision log before drafting ADR-0004. Native terminal commands never begin with !.
actions.rationale: The existing record establishes the occupied number and the byte prefix that P03 must preserve.
actions.expected_result: ADR-0003 remains occupied and the learner can identify the current log as the append-only prefix.
actions.recovery: If either artifact is missing or unexpectedly edited, stop and reset to a prepared baseline; do not recreate governance history by hand.
actions.evidence: The later log must retain the prepared decision-log bytes as its prefix.

actions.title: Request analysis, then make the exact choice
actions.instruction: Ask the agent to analyze the two alternatives and wait. The learner chooses and approves the ADR/log boundary; the agent may analyze and draft but may not select, replace, or broaden the choice.
actions.rationale: A comparison can make consequences legible without making an architecture decision on the learner's behalf.

actions.expected_result: The agent presents analysis, and the learner supplies one of the two exact choice statements before any ADR or log draft exists.
actions.recovery: If the agent chooses or writes before the learner sends one exact choice, preserve the attempt and reset instead of treating agent direction as learner evidence.
actions.evidence: The committed decision can match the selected statement, but Check cannot prove who sent it or why.

actions.title: Run the host-native ADR command after learner approval
actions.instruction: After the learner sends one exact choice and explicitly approves drafting the ADR/log boundary, invoke the selected host-native ADR command. The agent drafts the record; it does not decide for the learner.
actions.rationale: The shared CodeArbiter ADR lane creates a structured record while preserving learner authority over the content.
actions.expected_result: The agent drafts ADR-0004 and its matching log entry for the learner-approved boundary.
actions.recovery: If the command cannot preserve the learner-owned choice or writes a different boundary, stop and reset; do not hand-edit around the ADR lane.
actions.evidence: The host command is a drafting route, not proof that the learner approved the content.

actions.title: Run the host-native commit gate after approval
actions.instruction: After the learner reviews and explicitly approves the ADR/log content, invoke the selected host-native commit gate. Do not use a raw git commit as a substitute.
actions.rationale: The shared commit gate records the approved evidence through the supported host workflow.
actions.expected_result: One commit or two linear commits record only the approved ADR/log evidence, with ADR before log when split.
actions.recovery: If the gate blocks or the staged boundary includes another path, preserve the finding and reset; do not amend or force a commit.
actions.evidence: Git can show the resulting commit range and changed paths, but not the learner's approval process.

actions.title: Confirm native evidence at the clone root
actions.instruction: In a native terminal at the clone root, inspect the clean worktree, the latest one or two commits, and the ADR/log paths. Native terminal commands never begin with !.
actions.rationale: Native Git evidence makes the narrow committed boundary visible before Check reconstructs it.

variants.command:
git status --short
git log --format='%h %ad %an %s' --date=short -2
git diff --name-only HEAD~2..HEAD
git diff --check HEAD~2..HEAD

actions.expected_result: The worktree is clean and the visible range contains only the ADR and decision-log paths in the permitted ordering.
actions.recovery: If another path, a merge, an uncommitted change, or reversed ADR/log order appears, preserve the evidence and reset; do not rewrite the attempt.
actions.evidence: The native output exposes the same narrow final-state facts that Check can validate.

actions.title: Run installed Academy Check
actions.instruction: P03 is public in this preview. Run the installed Academy Check command from a native terminal.
actions.rationale: Check evaluates the committed evidence against the immutable P03 checkpoint rather than trusting a transcript.
actions.expected_result: Check reports whether the prepared evidence satisfies the immutable P03 checkpoint.
actions.recovery: If Check fails, preserve the predicate output and reset instead of amending, rebasing, or fabricating history.
actions.evidence: Check evaluates final committed artifacts and Git state, not a claimed live process.

actions.title: Preserve the failed attempt and reset
actions.instruction: P03 Reset is public in this preview. Run the installed Academy command from a native terminal only after preserving the failed evidence.
actions.rationale: Reset protects the failed attempt as evidence before restoring a new prepared baseline.
actions.expected_result: Academy archives the failed attempt and restores a fresh prepared baseline.
actions.recovery: If Reset is unavailable or fails, preserve the current attempt and do not delete the ADR, rewrite the log, or discard Git evidence.
actions.evidence: The archived attempt retains the evidence that explains why its checkpoint did not pass.
